entities.summary:
The Vienna State Opera is a historic opera house and opera company based in Vienna, Austria. The 1,709-seat Renaissance Revival venue was the first major building on the Vienna Ring Road. It was built from 1861 to 1869 following plans by August Sicard von Sicardsburg and Eduard van der Nüll, and designs by Josef Hlávka. The opera house was inaugurated as the "Vienna Court Opera" in the presence of Emperor Franz Joseph I and Empress Elisabeth of Austria.

It became known by its current name after the establishment of the First Austrian Republic in 1921. Vienna State Opera house is a opera house in Europe, established in 1869-05-25. historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Vienna State Opera house played a significant role in the development of opera and music culture in Europe during the late 19th century. Its establishment helped establish Vienna as a major center for musical innovation, with notable performances by composers such as Richard Wagner and Gustav Mahler.
